transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I feel constantly wound up and on edge, like I can’t relax even when I’m just at home with my family. My wife actually urged me to seek some help because it's starting to take a real toll on our relationship.

Did these feelings start after a specific stressful life event, or have they been ongoing without one? Also, do you ever get sudden intense panic attacks that peak within minutes with symptoms like racing heart, shortness of breath, or feeling like you might lose control?

This all started about nine months ago when my wife went back to work full-time and I took on a massive cloud migration project at my job. I don't really get those sudden, intense panic attacks with a racing heart or shortness of breath. It's more of a constant, ongoing feeling of being tightly wound and completely unable to relax.

Since those work and family changes nine months ago, have your symptoms stayed tied mainly to that stress, or do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of life even when those specific stressors aren’t the main issue? Have the symptoms continued even during times when things were going relatively smoothly?

It has definitely spread to almost every part of my life, even when things should be going smoothly. My brain constantly runs worst-case scenarios about everything from my parents' health to just planning dinner, and I can't shut off those "what-if" chains. Even when I'm trying to relax on the couch with my wife or play with the kids, I just can't stop the worry.

Along with the constant worry, have you also had symptoms like trouble sleeping, feeling restless or keyed up, muscle tension, getting tired easily, trouble concentrating, or being more irritable? Which of these have been happening most days?

Yes, I experience almost all of those on most days. I lie awake for hours replaying schedules, wake up around 3 a.m. unable to fall back asleep, and my body feels constantly tense with my shoulders up by my ears. I also struggle to concentrate at work, often losing my train of thought, and I've been so irritable lately that I keep snapping at my wife.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes excessive, difficult-to-control worry across multiple life domains, persisting most days for about nine months, with associated insomnia, restlessness/keyed-up feeling, muscle tension, impaired concentration, and irritability. Symptoms are generalized beyond the original stressors and continue even when things are going relatively smoothly, supporting generalized anxiety disorder rather than a stress-limited adjustment disorder. Panic attacks were denied.
